`lifecycleRules` takes an optional `shortStep` (Civ2 rolls only once a unit has moved, at remaining / cost), and `detonatedRules` an optional `vetoes` (Civ2's SDI Defense stops the whole attack). Both default to civ1-unit's behaviour. New tests cover the moved rules' cargo, collecting, disembarking, taking off and treaty breaking; the README notes what R2b must keep.
With civ1-unit's ids (pinned against civ1-unit 0.1.40's Rules/Unit/diplomat), so civ2-unit's Diplomats and Spies can establish embassies, investigate cities and meet leaders.

`lifecycleRules`, `movedRules` and `detonatedRules` build the rules from a prefix, the registries and the ruleset's options, with civ1-unit's ids and order (pinned against civ1-unit 0.1.40's own rules), so civ2-unit doesn't copy them and civ1-unit can adopt them later (R2b). `treatyPartner` is the partnerOf they and the treaty actions ask. Additive: no existing file changes.

unitDestroyed bought the replacement through PlayerTreasuryRegistry#getByPlayerAndType, which throws unless the player has exactly one Gold treasury. A ruleset with no treasury (Civ2's, until civ2-treasury) made the AI skip the unit's turn with 'Wrong number of playerTreasuries: 0'. It now buys only if the player has a Gold treasury; with exactly one, as in Civ1, it does the same as before.
